column2: req_desc

Start a claim without an account
From a phone with no account, the owner fills in the claim form, picks the model and the broken or missing part on the fitting fan, adds 1 to 4 damage photos, presses Start claim and the address bar moves to the claim's sent page.

Damage photos judged by their bytes
Each photo is accepted or refused only by its leading bytes and its size, with the edges in Business rules, and every refused file is named in its published message in the owner's language.

All-or-nothing claim start
A claim start stores the claim row, every photo and the reference together, or stores none of them, including when storage, mail or the claim records fail partway.

Carriage estimate while claiming
The claim form's carriage estimate comes only from the carrier's answer and shows the published state for a slow, failing or malformed answer without stopping the claim.

Confirmation email
Within 10 seconds of a claim start, Mailpit holds one message to the owner with the published subject, a one-time confirmation link and the link's closing time as the server set it.

Confirm from the email
Opening the emailed link and pressing Confirm my claim confirms the claim and moves the address bar to its share page, which shows the same state after a cold reload.

Confirmation link edges
The server accepts a confirmation link up to one second before its closing instant and refuses it at and after that instant, on a second use, and at once when the link lifetime setting is zero, each with its published status and message.

Operator sign-in
The seeded operator signs in and lands on the claim queue, and every operator page and endpoint refuses a caller without a live session, with the session edges in Business rules.

Identify the claimed part
The operator opens a confirmed claim, selects the part on the fitting fan, sets the quantity, presses Identify part and the address bar moves to the claim's quote stage with the ruling and deciding edition on the claim slip.

Aftercare term
The server rules a claim inside aftercare only when its confirmation instant is before the end of the term worked out from the purchase date, club membership and the deciding edition, with the edges and zero settings in Business rules.

Workshop business day
Every purchase date, term end, edition start, working day and dispatch cut-off is counted on the Europe/London calendar, never on UTC or the owner's device.

Clock-change Sundays
A claim confirmed on a day when Europe/London gains or loses an hour, or whose term ends on such a day, is ruled once under the published local-date rule.

Deciding edition
Each identified claim is ruled by the one edition in force at its confirmation instant, stores that edition's code, and shows it on every surface.

Decided-claims count
The operator's decided-claims count rises by one at each identification, splits into inside and outside, and never falls.

Keyboard-only identify and quote
The operator completes sign-in, identification, quoting and the decline dialog with the keyboard alone, with a visible focus ring on every focused control and Shift+Tab retracing each step.

Publish an aftercare edition
On the editions page the operator saves a dated edition whose start date the server accepts as later than today's London date, and sees it listed with its start date.

Editions never reach back
Saving an edition changes no existing ruling, and an edition rules only claims confirmed from 00:00 Europe/London on its start date.

Import the supplier parts file
On the imports page the operator uploads the supplier CSV and sees counts of new, updated, unchanged and unmatched rows, with each unmatched row listed by line number and reason.

Model name matching
Each import row's model name matches exactly one catalogue model under the published normalisation, code-suffix and retired-name rules, or is reported as unknown or ambiguous.

Import report and re-import
Every invalid row is reported with its line number and published reason, and importing the same file again creates and changes nothing.

Withdrawn parts
A withdrawn part can no longer be claimed, estimated, identified or re-quoted, while claims already quoting it keep their quoted figures and can still be dispatched.

Public parts list
The public parts list pages in a stable order, returns at most 50 parts per page, answers 429 with Retry-After once a caller exceeds the published rate, and refuses every request when the rate is zero.

Quote a claim
On an identified claim the operator presses Get quote once, the button stays disabled until the answer, and the address bar moves to the new quote revision's address with the part line, carriage line, total and dispatch promise on the slip.

Quote figures
The part line, carriage line and total are worked out in one place, rounded half-up to the penny, recorded as one Kill Bill invoice, and shown only as Kill Bill confirms them.

No quote without the carrier
A slow, failing or malformed carrier answer makes no quote, no invoice and no state change, and returns its published status.

Re-quote revisions
Re-quoting an unpaid claim voids the previous revision's invoice and adds the next numbered revision, which becomes the only current one while void revisions sit in the Earlier revisions disclosure.

Dispatch promise
Each quote carries either the same-working-day promise or a later dated promise, decided by the server from bin stock, working days and the dispatch cut-off, with the cut-off edge and zero setting in Business rules.

Record the owner's payment
Recording payment on a quoted claim records an external payment of the whole invoice in Kill Bill and shows the paid figure Kill Bill confirms.

Dispatch a part
On a paid quoted claim the operator presses Dispatch and the address bar moves to the claim's dispatched stage, with the dispatch note available from the slip.

Dispatch note
Each dispatch stores one server-rendered dispatch note in MinIO, and its lines and figures match the Kill Bill invoice and payment to the penny.

Bin stock
A quote that takes parts from the bin reserves them, a voided revision or a decline returns them, and a part short of stock is quoted as supplier-ordered.

Replayed billing actions
Quote, payment, decline and dispatch requests carry an idempotency key, a replay on the same claim returns the stored response with no second Kill Bill effect, and a reused key with a different body or action is refused.

Decline a claim
From a quoted claim the operator opens the Decline claim dialog, chooses a reason, confirms and the address bar moves to the claim's declined stage.

Decline without charge
Declining an unpaid claim voids its invoice in Kill Bill and shows the zero balance Kill Bill reports.

Refund when a part cannot be sent
Declining a paid claim refunds the whole payment in Kill Bill and shows the refunded figure Kill Bill confirms.

Close a claim
The operator closes a declined or dispatched claim, which ends its share link and sends the closed notice.

Owner notices
The quoted, declined, dispatched, closed and new-link notices reach the owner exactly once in the claim's language, with the published subjects, Kill Bill figures and no private field.

Follow a claim by share link
The owner follows the claim from confirmed through dispatch or decline on its share page, which shows the state, part, ruling, deciding edition, newest quote and dispatch promise, and which shows the owner refusal instead once the claim closes or the link is withdrawn.

Server-decided status on owner pages
The sent page, confirmation page and share page show link lifetime, ruling, cover end and dispatch promise exactly as the server decided them, whatever the device clock or time zone.

Share link shows one claim read-only
The share link returns one claim with no private field, and every attempt to change anything through it is refused.

Share link ends
The share link answers on the last request before the claim closes or the operator withdraws it and is refused on the first request after, and a new link sent by the operator replaces the old one.

Find my claim and reference lock
The owner reaches the share page with the right reference and email, a wrong pair gets the published not-found answer, and 5 wrong tries lock the reference behind its own message, with the lock edges and zero setting in Business rules.

Erase an owner
At the owner's request the operator erases them from a claim's workspace by typing its reference exactly as issued, untrimmed and letter case included, in the Erase owner data dialog, and every claim of that owner shows as erased.

Nothing left after erasure
After erasure no Postgres row, MinIO object or Mailpit message holds the owner's details, photos, notes or notices, and the decided-claims count is unchanged.

Boot with a service down
The desk starts and serves with MinIO, the carrier, Kill Bill, Mailpit or Postgres unreachable, and each affected action shows its published outage status and copy and leaves nothing behind.

Recover without a restart
Once an unreachable service answers again, the next action that needs it succeeds without restarting the desk.

Billing and mail outages
With Kill Bill unreachable no quote, payment or decline changes anything, and with Mailpit unreachable notices wait and are sent once it returns, as qualified in Services.

Exploded fitting fan
The fitting fan draws the model's parts in booklet order, spreads them along the model's axis by the published amounts as the slider moves, exposes its published attributes, and places each part on screen where those attributes say once the glide settles.

Fan by keyboard
The fan's slider answers the arrow, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End keys, parts take focus in booklet order, and Enter selects the focused part.

Fan on a phone with reduced motion
On a 375 px phone with reduced motion the fan opens fully separated at once with no glide, and tapping a part selects it through to the sent page.

Diagram unavailable list
A model whose diagram cannot be drawn shows its parts as a numbered list of buttons in booklet order under the published heading, with the selection attribute on the list and no slider in the accessibility tree.

Workspace and claim form breakpoints
The operator's claim workspace, including its pane shares at 1280 px, and the owner's claim form show their published layouts at 375, 768 and 1280 px wide with no sideways scrolling.

Run manifest and health
The desk installs, builds and serves from its run manifest on port 4173 and answers the health check with 200 and an ok status.

Role checks and private fields
Operator endpoints need a live session, owner endpoints never accept an operator action, a share token reads only its own claim, and no credential, database id, Kill Bill id or storage key reaches the browser.

Claim state machine
Every move outside the published state machine is refused with 409 and the current state, and each control is enabled only in states that allow it.

Two languages verbatim
Owner screens switch between English and Polish without moving the page by more than 1 px, and show every published string character for character in the chosen language.

Assembly-booklet look
Screens read as an assembly booklet spread: warm paper, a blueprint diagram on a faint grid, a ruled claim slip and mono part numbers.

Hairline callouts and source captions
Every diagram part carries a hairline callout to its booklet number, and every figure on the slip carries a small mono caption naming its source.

Settings and credentials from the environment
Every service URL, credential and desk setting is read from the environment at start, and is never written into source or sent to the browser.

Money read back from billing
Every amount the desk shows, renders into a note or emails is read back from Kill Bill, never kept from the desk's own arithmetic.

Claim records outage
With Postgres unreachable the desk still answers its health check and serves its pages, every action needing records answers 503 with the published copy, and the desk applies its schema as soon as Postgres answers.

Newest carriage estimate wins
The estimate region shows only the answer to the newest Estimate carriage press, and an older answer that arrives later is dropped.

Copies share state only through the records
Copies of the desk that share a database see the same claims, sessions, locks, rate windows, idempotency records and notice queue, and each waiting notice is sent exactly once by whichever copy reaches Mailpit.

Closed means unavailable
Closed dialogs, the collapsed Earlier revisions and Claim history disclosures, and the queue pane below 1280 px are hidden, unfocusable and absent from the accessibility tree at every viewport.

Fan shortcut and selection during the glide
Inside the fitting fan, ] and [ select the next and previous active part from whichever control has focus, and a second selection during the glide is the one that stays.

Published address after every action
After each owner and operator action the address bar shows the published address on its own, and a cold reload or deep link to it shows the same screen in the same state.

Share page updates in place
The share page shows the operator's newest changes within 35 seconds with no page load and the scroll position kept, keeps its content through a records outage, and removes it when the link ends.

Dialogs keep the newest state
Reopening the Decline claim or Erase owner data dialog during its fade-out leaves it open with focus on its first control, and no earlier timer closes it.

Announced refusals and retries
Every refusal is announced in the page's one alert region and every pending or waiting-notice message in its one status region, and a successful retry empties the stale alert.

Confirmation page layout
The confirmation page shows its published one-column layout, element order, widths and centring at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no sideways scrolling.

Confirmation agrees across records, mail and screen
After confirming, the Postgres claim row, the share page, the share API, the history entry, the sent page and the confirmation email agree on the state, the confirmation instant and the link's closing minute, as qualified in How this desk is checked.

Confirmation refuses other references as unknown
The confirmation status and confirm endpoints answer another owner's, an erased or a malformed reference, or a body reference naming a different claim, byte for byte like an unknown one before any validation error, and change nothing.

Decline dialog layout over a still workspace
The Decline claim dialog shows its published layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800, and opening it moves no workspace pane by more than 1 px.

Decline figures agree with billing on every surface
A decline's zero charge or refund on the slip, the share page and the declined notice equals the void invoice and balance or the REFUND transaction amount Kill Bill reports, in the claim's language format.

Decline stock and key edges
A decline returns bin stock exactly once at the published stock edge, and the decline's idempotency key follows the published length, character and per-claim scope edges.

Operator claim actions refuse other references as unknown
Every operator claim action answers another owner's or a malformed reference, or a body reference naming a different claim, byte for byte like an unknown one before any validation error, and changes nothing in Postgres, Kill Bill or Mailpit.

Share and find page layouts
The share page and the Find my claim page show their published layouts, element order, column count and widths at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no sideways scrolling.

Share page agrees with billing, note and notice
The share page's part, carriage, total and paid lines equal the current Kill Bill invoice and payment, the stored dispatch note and the newest quoted notice to the penny, with void revisions absent.

Find and share refuse other references as unknown
Find my claim and the share endpoint answer another owner's, an erased or a malformed reference byte for byte like an unknown one, count wrong tries only against the reference named, and change nothing.

Erase dialog layout
The Erase owner data dialog shows its published layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800, and opening it moves no workspace pane by more than 1 px.

Erasure leaves exactly the published remains
After erasure Postgres, MinIO, Mailpit and Kill Bill each hold exactly the published remains for every claim of that owner in any state, every other address's mail is kept, and a second erase is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

Erasure refuses other references as unknown
The erase endpoint answers another owner's or a malformed reference, or a body reference naming a different claim, byte for byte like an unknown one before any validation error, and erases nothing.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package, the bundled typefaces and the Lucide icons, each with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package and asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The desk stores data only in the provided Postgres and MinIO: no SQLite, no other database or cache, no in-process store of shared state, and no local files used as a datastore.
The provided service configuration and dev compose files are left unchanged.
All server and browser source is TypeScript.
